paper.title: SkillWeaver: Web Agents can Self-Improve by Discovering and Honing Skills
paper.central_claim: A web agent can self-improve without parameter updates by autonomously proposing skills for a new website, practising them, synthesizing them into Python/Playwright APIs and honing them with tests; the resulting library raises success on WebArena (relative +31.8%) and on live websites (+39.8%) and transfers to weaker agents (up to +54.3%).

provenance.notes: Opus aggregate seat via the configured claude-kimi type fable; no route probing. actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref are null because the subagent runtime exposes no verifiable provider receipt to this worker.

sections_read: Opus: complete pinned text read end-to-end (abstract, all sections, tables, appendices) before opening seat records; targeted re-reads for every disputed field

evidence.quote: Given a new website, the agent autonomously discovers skills, executes them for practice, and distills practice experiences into robust APIs.
evidence.support_explanation: Core loop: self-proposed skill tasks, practice, API synthesis; no test queries or demonstrations are used.

evidence.support_explanation: Curriculum is a prompted LLM proposal of procedural, navigational and information-seeking tasks conditioned on the skill library and observations; no measured test that the novelty prompting or simple-to-complex progression matters.

evidence.support_explanation: Admission of a practised trajectory is decided by an LLM reward model (task, trajectory with screenshots, execution feedback); its accuracy is not measured.

evidence.quote: from successful trajectories into a reusable and generalized API.
evidence.support_explanation: Successful trajectories are converted to Python functions with signature, docstring, usage log and prerequisite-state description; a static analyser rejects common generation mistakes.

evidence.quote: For APIs requiring no extra parameters except the by default Playwright page instance, we execute the API directly as a standalone unit test.
evidence.support_explanation: Honing executes each API as a unit test (with LLM-generated parameter values where needed) and debugs it from feedback.

evidence.quote: iterations with GPT-4o, where an iteration is defined as either attempting a proposed skill or testing an existing skill.
evidence.support_explanation: Exploration budget: 160 iterations per website with GPT-4o, run per website separately before evaluation; during exploration the agent can call earlier APIs to compose new ones.

signatures.object: Per-website skill library of async Python/Playwright APIs with docstrings (usage log, pre-conditions); baseline is the CodeAct agent with atomic browser actions only.
signatures.information: Screenshots, accessibility tree, URL and page state; own prior skill list and semantic knowledge notes; LLM-judged success; execution exceptions. No test queries or demonstrations.
signatures.operation: (I) LLM proposes a new short-horizon skill task (procedural, navigational, information-seeking) beyond the current repertoire; (II) agent attempts it, LLM reward model judges success, successful trajectories are converted to an API and statically checked; (III) each API is run as a unit test with LLM-chosen parameters and debugged; docstrings are updated after later attempts.
signatures.output: Library of callable skills, 160 exploration iterations per website with GPT-4o, composable by later skills.
signatures.conditions: Website where short, reusable procedures exist; LLM judge and test inputs adequate; agent able to call APIs.
signatures.feedback: LLM reward on trajectories; Python exceptions and environment feedback in honing.
signatures.selection_rule: Retain if the reward model says success and the API runs without exception in the unit test; update by function-name replacement.
signatures.persistence: Library files per website, reused at inference via an API selection module that filters by relevance and pre-conditions; shareable across agents.
signatures.later_use: Skills added to the agent's action space at evaluation time and also used in later exploration for composition.
signatures.claimed_effect: WebArena avg 22.6 to 29.8 (GPT-4o) and 9.2 to 14.1 (GPT-4o-mini); live 23 to 32 of 57 tasks.
signatures.failure_boundary: Exception-free is accepted as verified (D.2.1); no realistic test inputs for data-dependent skills (D.2.2); weak LLMs mis-select or mis-parameterise APIs; high-API-support sites favour human APIs.

signatures.object: Skill-use interface: API selection module that filters the library per task and checks pre-conditions.
signatures.information: Task description, current state, skill signatures and docstrings.
signatures.operation: LLM selects candidate functions and injects 'signature + docstring' into the prompt.
signatures.output: Task-conditioned skill list for the acting agent.
signatures.conditions: Library too large for full inclusion.
signatures.claimed_effect: Enables use of a large library; not ablated.
signatures.failure_boundary: Failure to call available APIs (D.2.4) and wrong parameters (D.2.5).

gap.author_gap: Web agents lack autonomous self-improvement: trajectory-memory and fine-tuning approaches do not abstract reusable procedures and are heavy to share; AWM and ICAL use natural-language routines that resist verification and composition and depend on test queries or annotated demonstrations.
gap.checked_gap: The target is specific: label-free, query-free exploration producing verifiable, composable, shareable artifacts. The protocol difference from AWM/ICAL is real, but those neighbours (and the concurrent ASI work of overlapping authors) are not run, and the quantified headroom is only the skills-off baseline.
gap.lineage: Voyager-style skill libraries and LLM curricula -> Agent Workflow Memory / ICAL (text routines) -> SkillWeaver (self-proposed tasks, verified executable APIs, portability). Comparisons are to AutoEval and SteP using published numbers. Neighbours cited, not available as fixed local sources.
gap.closest_adjacent: AWM, ICAL, Synapse (trajectory exemplars), Voyager, AutoEval, SteP.
gap.residue: Reliable verification of synthesized skills, test inputs for data-dependent skills, robust skill calling, high-API-support sites.
gap.stakes: Adaptation of web agents to unfamiliar websites without supervision or parameter updates.
gap.method_response: Executable API artifacts built by a propose-practise-synthesise-hone loop and shared across agents.
gap.remaining_gap: Verification relies on exception-free runs and an LLM judge; skill-use failures dominate the residual errors; cost is unmeasured.
unresolved: Whether AWM/ICAL-style or test-time retry baselines at equal exploration compute match the library could not be checked from fixed local sources.

rs_pattern.reason: Same ruling as 2504.06821: Playwright API programs are C25's machine-checkable artifacts, executed as unit tests in a verify-and-revise loop; no proved property preservation for operator substitution.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Step 2 machine-checkable intermediate artifact: Python/Playwright APIs executed as tests, present. Step 3 close the loop with verifiable output during construction: unit-test execution and exception feedback, but success is also judged by an LLM reward model and exception-free is a weak oracle. Step 4 ablate the verification step: absent. Step 5 cost accounting and validation beyond toy instances: cost absent; WebArena plus live sites present. Step 1 boundary between learned model and sound solver: only the Python/browser runtime is sound.
matches.success_failure_checks: Success: executable typed handoff artifacts, closed feedback loop, growing reusable library, transfer across agents. Failure: delegated-step cost never measured; honing not ablated; verifier weak.
matches.reason: The load-bearing object is a checkable executable artifact. self_supervised_signal_engineering/C08 was read and rejected: its object is a filtered training instance set that is retrained on, while here nothing is trained and the output is a skill library.

rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial: library on/off +7.2 points WebArena, +9/57 live

condition_checks: S1 admission gate is execution not judgment: partial (LLM reward plus exception-free unit test)
S2 admit only capability increments: partial (novelty prompting, no re-derivability test)
S3 abstraction validated beyond source instance: partial (LLM-generated test parameters, cross-agent and live-site use)
S4 repair driven by obtainable signals: met (error-driven debugging, Appendix D.1.2)
S5 retained library shown to carry the gain: met (skills on/off on WebArena and live)
H06-step1 practice source disjoint from evaluation: met (task-agnostic exploration)

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Executable skill APIs verified by running them (RS artifact-plus-checker) correspond to H06's self-directed practice with execution-gated admission into a growing library.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: H06 needs a gate stronger than a judge and full construction cost; here the checker accepts exception-free runs and an LLM judge, and cost is absent. C25 needs a sound solver and ablation of the verification step; neither is fully present.

claims.text: Synthesized APIs raise WebArena success for a GPT-4o web agent.
claims.setting: Table 1, five WebArena sites, 812 tasks, CodeAct agent, GPT-4o temperature 0.3
claims.selection_vs_test: library built by task-agnostic exploration, tasks unseen
claims.result_denominator: avg 22.6 to 29.8; per-site gains 4.4-12.3 points; one run
claims.allowed_conclusion: A pre-built library lifts a fixed agent by about 7 points average on unseen WebArena tasks; the relative-gain figures in the text are inconsistent; SteP is higher overall.

claims.text: Skills improve success on live websites.
claims.setting: Table 2, 57 Online-Mind2Web tasks on 4 sites, manual judging
claims.allowed_conclusion: Net +9 tasks of 57 in one run, manually judged, no significance test.

claims.text: Synthesized APIs from a strong agent transfer to a weaker agent.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Skill library built by a stronger model helps a weaker executor on WebArena.

claims.text: Synthesized APIs match human-crafted APIs on low- and medium-support sites.
claims.result_denominator: figure only, no numbers in text
claims.allowed_conclusion: Not verifiable from the text-only material; author statement only.

claims.text: Skills discovered and honed autonomously are reliable.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Reliability is not shown; the authors document exception-silencing APIs passing verification.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Library built by task-agnostic exploration, frozen, then used on unseen WebArena and live tasks and by a weaker agent; same-agent skills on/off isolates the library as a whole.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Single runs: the pre-built library lifts the same GPT-4o agent 22.6→29.8 on WebArena (+31.9% rel), 23→32 of 57 manually judged live tasks, and GPT-4o-mini 9.2→14.1 (+53.3% rel; paper prints 45% and 54.3%). 'Robust' APIs are not established (exception-free acceptance, opus:O04); SteP is higher overall; the role of proposal/reward/honing stages and exploration cost are not shown.

G.reason: Opus sides with sol. The fixed objects (trajectory demonstrations, unverifiable text routines, test-query access in AWM/ICAL) and the residual problem (query-free autonomous skill acquisition) are concrete with Voyager/Friday/AWM lineage. Not 4: neighbours compared via external numbers only — charged under E.causality, as for 2504.00185 and 2504.06821.

M.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Propose–practise–synthesise–hone is coherent, but the assumptions that the novelty curriculum and LLM reward select good skills are untested and the honing check accepts exception-free code (opus:O04). This gate weakness is charged here once.

X.reason: Opus sides with son55. Every stage is reconstructable from full prompts (proposal, action synthesis, success check, persistence, scraping, retrieval), the library format carries pre-conditions and usage logs, and failure modes are reported openly; retirement, versioning, size and state reset absent. The weak gate is not charged twice (it is in M).

E.measurement.reason: Opus sides with sol. The 812-task WebArena checker is credible, but the scored denominator is ambiguous (764 per-site vs 812, opus:O03), live results are author-judged without blinding, and headline relative gains disagree across abstract, §4.1 and Table 1 (opus:O01, opus:O02). Unlike 2504.06821 the inconsistencies sit in the headline gain figures.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Skills on/off on two agents and two benchmarks is a clean store-off control; no stage ablation, no equal-compute alternative, external-number comparisons (SteP higher overall).
